blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: The case study this topic requires: settlement and service provision in one area, the corridor of towns in the Oshana region of northern Namibia.

blocks.heading: The Oshana corridor
blocks.text: Three fast-growing towns sit within about 30 kilometres of each other in the Oshana region: Oshakati, about 59 000 people (2023); Ongwediva, about 34 000; and Ondangwa, about 30 000. Around and between them lies one of the densest farmed landscapes in Namibia, a rural population of about 230 000 (2023) whose homesteads and mahangu fields fill the ground the towns have not taken. The towns live by serving that countryside. Oshakati began as an administrative and market centre and was proclaimed a town in 1992; Ondangwa grew at the railway and road junction; Ongwediva is the newest, an administrative and shopping centre. Each town's sphere of influence runs deep into the surrounding villages, and each day the buses and pickups of those villages bring people to the towns' services.

blocks.heading: Services and thresholds in the corridor
blocks.text: Walk up the corridor's ladder and the services sort as the hierarchy predicts. The villages keep a clinic, a primary school and small shops, services a few hundred people can support. Each town holds secondary schools, filling stations, banks and wholesalers. The highest order concentrates: only Oshakati holds the intermediate hospital, which serves patients from across the north, and only Ondangwa holds the airport. Oshakati's open market, hundreds of stalls trading grain, clothes and livestock goods, shows a large threshold at work: no village could gather enough traders and buyers to pay for it, so the market stands where the whole sphere of influence can reach it in a day. Service provision here is the hierarchy of the first half of this topic, printed onto one small area of the map.

blocks.heading: Where this connects
blocks.text: This case study answers any question that names an area of settlement and service provision; its hierarchy is 1.5.1's ladder on the ground, and its fast-growing towns return in topic 1.7.
